task: Review every supplied part, discover the most consequential events from the supplied evidence, cluster related reports, assign the best-fit broad news category dynamically and produce up to 150 processed stories using schema/processed-news.schema.json. The final portfolio must contain at least five well-supported stories in every category. Treat social attention as a discovery signal rather than verification. More than half of the final stories must originate with independent, local or social discovery, using the first source in each story as the discovery source; established outlets may account for no more than half.

items.title: Bengaluru: EPFO official’s death triggers anger over road conditions
items.summary: A 32-year-old central government employee with the Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) in Bengaluru was killed on Thursday, August 13, following a vehicle accident while travelling to work. Medha Akarsh from Kerala, was riding pillion with her colleague on a two-wheeler on Ananth Nagar Main Road, near Electronics City Phase II, when she met with the mishap. According to reports , a car ahead suddenly braked after a pedestrian moved towards the middle of the road. The two-wheeler rider also braked, causing the scooter to skid on a slushy, damaged stretch of road. Medha was thrown onto the road and into the path of an approaching mini goods vehicle. She was rushed to a private hospital but succumbed to her injuries. The mishap occurred around 3 km from her home, reports said. She leaves behind her husband and three-year-old son. Following the accident, residents blamed the poor condition of the road for the mishap. According to a Times of India report , residents said the stretch had remained in poor condition for years, with potholes, waterlogging and damaged road surfaces making daily commuting hazardous. Residents held a candlelight march at Ananth Nagar on Wednesday eve
